en: A, as its first of letters, every speech maintains;
The "Primal Deity" is first through all the world’s domains
1.s: As the letter ‘A’ comes first in every language, the Divine comes first in the world. Begin from what is highest.

en: No fruit have men of all their studied lore,
Save they the ‘Purely Wise One’s’ feet adore
2.s: What is the use of all your learning if you never bow to true wisdom?

en: His foot, ‘Whom want affects not, irks not grief,’ who gain
Shall not, through every time, of any woes complain
4.s: Those who reach the One who wants nothing and fears nothing will never face trouble anywhere.

en: Unless His foot, ‘to Whom none can compare,’ men gain,
‘Tis hard for mind to find relief from anxious pain
7.s: Worry will not leave the mind until it finds a greater, steadier thing to hold on to.

en: They swim the sea of births, the ‘Monarch’s’ foot who gain;
None others reach the shore of being’s mighty main
10.s: Only those who hold on to the highest will cross the great ocean of life. The rest will not reach the other shore.

en: The world its course maintains through life that rain unfailing gives;
Thus rain is known the true ambrosial food of all that lives
11.s: Rain keeps every living thing alive. It is the world’s own food — treasure it.

en: When water fails, functions of nature cease, you say;
Thus when rain fails, no men can walk in ‘duty’s ordered way’
20.s: Without water, nothing in nature works. Without rain, people cannot even live good and orderly lives.

en: To finish virtue’s work with ceaseless effort strive,
What way thou may’st, where’er thou see’st the work may thrive
33.s: Do good in every way you can, at every chance you get. Never stop trying.

en: ‘Tis never good to let the thought of good things done thee pass away;
Of things not good, ‘tis good to rid thy memory that very day
108.s: Never forget a kindness done to you. Forget any harm on the very same day.

en: As earth bears up the men who delve into her breast,
To bear with scornful men of virtues is the best
151.s: The earth holds up even the people who dig it. In the same way, bear with those who insult you. That is the greatest virtue.

en: Forgiving trespasses is good always;
Forgetting them hath even higher praise
152.s: Forgiving someone is always good. Forgetting the hurt is even better.

en: Who wreak their wrath as worthless are despised;
Who patiently forbear as gold are prized
155.s: People who lash out in anger are thrown away like trash. Patient people are kept safe like gold.

en: Though others work thee ill, thus shalt thou blessing reap;
Grieve for their sin, thyself from vicious action keep
157.s: Even if others do you wrong, do not do wrong back. Feel sorry for their mistake, and stay good.

en: You ask, in lips of men what ‘truth’ may be;
‘Tis speech from every taint of evil free
291.s: What is truth? It is words with no harm in them at all.

en: Speak not a word which false thy own heart knows
Self-kindled fire within the false one’s spirit glows
293.s: Never say what you know in your heart is false. A lie burns the liar first.

en: If all your life be utter truth, the truth alone,
‘Tis well, though other virtuous acts be left undone
297.s: If you live by truth alone, that is enough. Even if you do nothing else good, truth is enough.

en: If thou would’st guard thyself, guard against wrath alway;
‘Gainst wrath who guards not, him his wrath shall slay
305.s: If you want to protect yourself, guard against anger. Anger will kill the one who does not control it.

en: Though unprovoked thy soul malicious foes should sting,
Retaliation wrought inevitable woes will bring
313.s: Even if enemies hurt you for no reason, hurting them back will bring you ruin.

en: To punish wrong, with kindly benefits the doers ply;
Thus shame their souls; but pass the ill unheeded by
314.s: The best way to punish someone who hurts you: do them a kindness so good that they feel ashamed. Then let the harm go.

en: What his own soul has felt as bitter pain,
From making others feel should man abstain
316.s: If you know in your own heart what hurts, do not do it to anyone else. That is the whole rule.

en: Lowest and meanest lore, that bids men trust secure,
In things that pass away, as things that shall endure
331.s: The worst kind of foolishness: trusting things that pass as if they will last forever.

en: As ‘day’ it vaunts itself; well understood, ‘tis knife,
That daily cuts away a portion from thy life
334.s: It calls itself ‘day,’ but it is really a knife. Every day it quietly cuts a piece of your life away.

en: No glorious wealth is here like freedom from desire;
To bliss like this not even there can soul aspire
363.s: The greatest wealth in this world is to want nothing. Nothing in any world is better than that.

en: Affliction is not known where no desires abide;
Where these are, endless rises sorrow’s tide
368.s: Where there is no craving, there is no sorrow. Where craving stays, sorrow keeps growing.

en: When good things come, men view them all as gain;
When evils come, why then should they complain
379.s: When good things come, people call it fortune. When hard times come, why blame fortune?

en: The twain that lore of numbers and of letters give
Are eyes, the wise declare, to all on earth that live
392.s: Numbers and letters together are like eyes for people. Learning opens your sight.

en: In sandy soil, when deep you delve, you reach the springs below;
The more you learn, the freer streams of wisdom flow
396.s: Dig deep in sand and water springs up. The more you learn, the more wisdom flows.

en: Though fate-divine should make your labour vain;
Effort its labour’s sure reward will gain
619.s: Even if fate blocks the result, honest effort still pays its own reward.

en: All men that live are one in circumstances of birth;
Diversities of works give each his special worth
972.s: Every person is born the same. Only what they do makes them different.
